one_line: Rana Kumbha of Mewar and Sultan Mahmud Khalji of Malwa at the turning-point battles around Sarangpur, 1437 CE.

appearance.age_look: both appear in their late 30s to early 40s, tall and martial, with sturdy builds
appearance.face: Kumbha has a long, strong-jawed face with sharp nose, wheatish-olive Rajput complexion, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard, with a calm but intense default expression; Mahmud has a slightly rounder face, medium-brown complexion, trimmed moustache and pointed beard, keen eyes and a proud, watchful default expression.
appearance.hair: Kumbha’s black hair is medium length, tied back in a low knot under a red velvet Rajput-style turban with a golden band and a single white egret plume; Mahmud’s black hair is mostly hidden under a dark green conical Malwa-Sultanate turban wrapped over a quilted cap, with a small gold finial at the peak.
appearance.costume: Rana Kumbha wears a fitted quilted cotton angarkha in deep maroon with narrow golden border lines, over a mail shirt hinted at the collar and sleeves, a mustard-yellow sash at the waist, and off-white churidar trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots; over this he has a light steel chest-plate with simple etched floral edges and a soft cream shawl with subtle red motifs draped over his left shoulder; he wears minimal gold earrings, a simple armlet on his right arm and a small tilak on his forehead; Mahmud Khalji wears a knee-length dark green, slightly flared quilted coat (qabā) with fine gold piping and a front opening, over visible mail at the neckline, with a wide dark red cloth belt, straight cream trousers, and dark brown leather boots, plus a steel lamellar overcoat suggested by overlapping plate segments on the chest and shoulders; his turban is dark green with narrow gold bands, and he has a short dark cloak hanging to mid-thigh from his shoulders, with restrained geometric trim at the edges.
appearance.signature: Kumbha carries a long straight Rajput sword with a gently flared tip and a traditional Indo-Muslim hilt in steel and brass at his left hip, plus a large round steel shield slung on his back; Mahmud carries a slightly curved Indo-Persian saber with a dark leather scabbard and a small round buckler strapped to his left forearm.

ref_desc: Rana Kumbha has a long-jawed face, wheatish complexion, black hair in a low knot under a red turban with white plume, maroon quilted angarkha over mail, mustard sash, off-white churidar and boots with sword and round shield, while Mahmud Khalji has a medium-brown face with trimmed beard, dark green conical turban, dark green quilted coat and lamellar over mail, cream trousers, cloak, curved saber and buckler, all in deep maroon, mustard yellow, dark green, cream and steel grey tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet showing two distinct but equally dignified 15th-century Indian warrior rulers side by side: Rana Kumbha and Mahmud Khalji, from the Mewar–Malwa wars around 1437 CE, in historically grounded armour and clothing. Rana Kumbha is tall and sturdy with a long, strong-jawed face, wheatish-olive complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard, black hair tied in a low knot, wearing a red velvet Rajput-style turban with a golden band and a single white egret plume. His outfit is a fitted deep maroon quilted cotton angarkha with narrow golden border lines, worn over a hinted mail shirt at collar and sleeves, a mustard-yellow sash at the waist, and off-white churidar trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots; over this is a plain steel chest-plate with subtle floral edging and a soft cream shawl with discrete red motifs draped over his left shoulder, plus small gold earrings, a simple armlet and a tilak on his forehead. He carries a long straight Rajput sword with a slightly flared tip and traditional steel-and-brass hilt at his left hip and a large round steel shield slung on his back. Beside him, Mahmud Khalji stands as a rival sultan: medium-brown complexion, slightly rounder face with keen eyes, trimmed moustache and pointed beard, wearing a dark green conical Malwa-Sultanate turban wrapped over a quilted cap with a small gold finial at the top. His costume is a knee-length dark green slightly flared quilted coat (qabā) with fine gold piping and a front opening, over visible mail at the neckline, with a wide dark red cloth belt, straight cream trousers and dark brown leather boots, plus a steel lamellar overcoat suggested by overlapping plates on the chest and shoulders and a short dark cloak with simple geometric trim to mid-thigh. He grips a slightly curved Indo-Persian saber in a dark leather scabbard and has a small round buckler strapped to his left forearm. Use a limited palette dominated by deep maroon, mustard yellow, dark green, cream and steel grey, and present both characters front-facing in neutral but battle-ready poses so their face shapes, hairstyles, costumes and weapons can be consistently redrawn.
